signals.signal: FY2025 results (published 30/04/2026) re-confirm the estate at 31/12/2025: 1,220 ATMs and 264 MFMs (1,484 units), POS estate +25.8% vs 2024, digital-infrastructure investment ~RON 235m in 2025, #3 in Romania by number of devices. Card transactions +27% by count / +25.3% by value; POS transaction volumes +49% by count and +88% by value. Group net profit RON 815.1m, total capital ratio 31.2%, cost/income 48.6%.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Grupul Financiar CEC Bank: Rezultate financiare pentru anul 2025
signals.implies: Only 264 of 1,484 units are deposit-capable multifunction machines - the largest cash-recycler white space in Romania; explosive POS growth supports acquiring/terminal-estate and managed-services propositions.
signals.likelihood: High - modernisation is a standing multi-year programme
signals.followup: Name the ATM/MFM OEM and the maintenance incumbent; quantify how many of the 264 MFMs are true recyclers vs deposit-only.

signals.signal: Pillar 3 / transparency report for 2025 (uploaded to cec.ro in July 2026) states that at 31/12/2025 the bank operated 46 directorates/independent services, 1,011 territorial units and had 4,893 employees (4,887 FTE + 6 part-time).
signals.source_name: CEC Bank - Raport privind cerintele de transparenta si publicare 2025 (PDF)
signals.implies: A hard denominator for the branch-automation opportunity: 1,011 sites vs 1,484 machines is barely 1.5 devices per unit, and management says units will be converted rather than closed - i.e. an in-branch TCR/recycler and self-service-zone rollout of potentially 1,000+ sites.
signals.followup: Ask for the split of the 1,011 units by format (sucursala / agentie / punct de lucru) to size the in-branch recycler addressable base.

signals.signal: Romania's Competition Council announced on 07/06/2026 record fines of RON 3.73bn (c.EUR 710m) on 10 banks for coordinating conduct in the ROBOR fixing procedure; CEC Bank's share is RON 332.98m. CEC publicly rejected the decision on 08/06/2026 and said it will litigate, including before European courts.
signals.source_name: Economedia (live blog, incl. per-bank fine table) / CEC Bank statement
signals.implies: RON 332.98m equals roughly 41% of FY2025 net profit. Expect provisioning pressure and tighter scrutiny of 2026-27 discretionary capex - argue opex/managed-service and as-a-service commercial models rather than capex hardware purchases.
signals.followup: Watch for the provision in the H1-2026 interim accounts (usually published Oct) and for the published decision text on consiliulconcurentei.ro.

signals.signal: On 16/07/2026 CEC Bank launched Incasari Instant in euro (incoming instant euro credit transfers, 24/7 including weekends/holidays) for retail and corporate customers. Under the EU Instant Payments Regulation, non-euro-area PSPs must be able to RECEIVE instant euro by 09/01/2027 and to SEND, plus run Verification of Payee, by 09/07/2027.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank press release + ECB/IPR timetable
signals.implies: Receive-side is done ~6 months early; the send-side plus Verification of Payee and the associated 24/7 real-time fraud screening are still open and due 09/07/2027 - a direct opening for transaction-monitoring/AML and payment-fraud tooling.
signals.likelihood: Certain - it is a regulatory deadline
signals.followup: Ask who supplies the instant-payments fraud/sanctions screening layer, and whether Temenos Payments covers VoP or a third party is being sourced.

signals.signal: The five pilot Digital Agencies (Simeria/HD, Tibanesti/IS, Mioveni/AG, Jurilovca/TL, Floresti/CJ) launched 05/06/2026 combine 24/7 self-service equipment doing cash withdrawals AND cash deposits, FX exchange, payments, transfers and personal-data updates, with remote human help by videobanking for account opening, lending and e-signature. As of the product page last updated 26/06/2026 the count is still five; the bank says it will analyse results and feedback before extending the concept to other localities, with no target number and no date given.
signals.source_name: CEC Bank press release + Agentia Digitala product page
signals.implies: The functional spec (cash in + cash out + FX + bill payment in one lobby) is a recycler/multifunction-kiosk spec. A pilot-to-rollout decision is imminent and is the single highest-value entry point for self-service hardware, cash automation, videobanking-linked eKYC and managed services.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that a rollout decision lands within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Get the pilot equipment list and vendor; time an approach to the post-pilot review with a per-site TCO for a recycler + FX kiosk + videobanking pod.

signals.signal: Mugur Podaru, Director of Remote Operations, said on 06/04/2026 that CEC Bank is NOT closing agencies - it has already started building self-service units equipped with all the necessary machines inside its premises, keeping the digital direction while changing the agency architecture, across a network of over 1,000 branches and territorial units. No conversion target or timeline was given.
signals.source_name: Wall-Street.ro interview with CEC Bank management
signals.implies: CEC is the one Romanian bank converting rather than shrinking its network - the opposite of BRD/BCR. Every converted unit needs a recycler or deposit-capable machine plus a self-service zone; this is the largest single-bank branch-automation pipeline in the country.
signals.followup: Request a meeting with Directia Operatiuni la Distanta; ask for the 2027 unit-conversion plan and whether equipment is bought or leased.

signals.signal: Eighteen months after selecting Temenos (announced 15/01/2025, with SoftCentric and Tech Mahindra as delivery partners, including Temenos Payments for all domestic and cross-border payments), no go-live, phase completion or migration date has been announced by the bank, Temenos, SoftCentric or Tech Mahindra. The only 2026 status statement is the FY2025 report's line that the transformation 'advanced significantly, both in CRM implementation and in the new Core Banking System and related platforms'.
signals.source_name: Temenos press release (selection) + CEC Bank FY2025 results
signals.implies: A core migration still in flight means channel/device integration work (ATM/MFM host interfaces, POS/acquiring, card management) is being re-specified now - the right moment to position ATM middleware, device-driving software and integration/managed services before the cutover freezes the architecture.
signals.likelihood: Medium - a first go-live plausibly in 2026-27
signals.followup: Probe Temenos/SoftCentric/Tech Mahindra channels for the phasing and the planned ATM/self-service integration layer; watch Temenos quarterly results for a CEC go-live reference.

signals.entity: CEC Bank / all ATM operators in Romania
signals.signal: Legislative proposal B409/2026, amending Law 209/2019 on payment services, was registered at the Senate on 24/06/2026 (Legislative Council opinion 679 dated 22/07/2026, status 'registered at the Senate for debate'). It would oblige every payment service provider operating ATMs in Romania to let users enter a personalised withdrawal amount regardless of the card-issuing bank, with fines reported at RON 50,000-100,000 for non-compliance. It is signed by ~80 deputies across PSD, AUR, UDMR, USR, PNL and others.
signals.source_name: Senate of Romania - legislative file B409/2026
signals.implies: If adopted, every one of CEC's 1,484 ATMs/MFMs needs an application/interface change and re-certification - a concrete, deadline-driven ATM software and managed-services engagement across the whole Romanian market, not just CEC.
signals.likelihood: Medium - broad cross-party sponsorship but still first-chamber stage
signals.followup: Track the Senate vote and the transition period in the final text; prepare a market-wide ATM-application compliance offer.

signals.signal: CEC Bank runs its own open tender channel (not SEAP/SICAP) and publishes calls at cec.ro/achizitii, with offers filed at the Calea Victoriei 13 registry and enquiries to the Independent Procurement Service (sia@cec.ro). Two recent procedures: an IT messaging (Info SMS) solution, offers due 13/03/2026 then re-run to 23/04/2026; and physical-security risk analyses for CEC Bank sites, offers due 23/04/2026, with an annex listing the bank's sites as at 31/10/2025.
signals.implies: A monitorable, low-friction route in: CEC awards by open competitive tender on its own website, so ATM/cash-automation/security lots will surface here first. The security risk-analysis annex is also a free public inventory of the bank's physical estate.
signals.likelihood: High - the channel is live and reused
signals.followup: Poll cec.ro/achizitii weekly; register with sia@cec.ro as a qualified supplier for self-service, cash automation and security lots.

signals.signal: The ATM/MFM OEM has never been disclosed. The multi-year replacement programme started 21/07/2020 (EUR 2.6m in 2020, first 200 units), the supplier was 'one of the largest global producers' picked by competitive tender among the main national distributors, and by 17/05/2023 c.1,100 units had been replaced (>80% of the fleet), all with touchscreens, contactless and barcode/QR readers. MFMs accept RON and EUR cash deposits, do FX exchange and take bill payments in cash and by card. Separately, the integrated system for MONITORING AND MAINTENANCE of the bank's ATM and POS fleet was built in-house on the Aurachain low-code platform (announced 25/02/2021), alongside SME online onboarding and online trade finance.
signals.implies: Two things for Printec: (a) the hardware incumbent is deliberately unnamed and was won through open tender - so it is contestable at the next refresh cycle; (b) fleet monitoring/maintenance orchestration is INSIDE the bank on low-code, so a managed-services pitch must integrate with, not replace, that layer.
signals.likelihood: Medium - next refresh wave due as 2020-23 units age out from 2027
signals.followup: Identify the OEM/distributor from field photos or the 2020-2023 tender award; check whether the Aurachain fleet-monitoring app survived the Temenos programme.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed). Angles used: (1) cec.ro primary - press releases, product pages, procurement page and XML sitemap crawled with a desktop User-Agent to defeat the 403; (2) CEC investor-relations PDF library, including the newly posted 2025 Pillar 3/transparency report, which yielded the 1,011 units / 4,893 staff figures; (3) Romanian Parliament primary source (senat.ro legislative file B409/2026) for the ATM custom-amount bill - a source environment not used for this bank before; (4) competition-enforcement angle (Competition Council ROBOR decision, per-bank fine table); (5) EU Instant Payments Regulation timetable mapped onto CEC's 16/07/2026 euro instant-receive launch; (6) vendor-side checks on Temenos, SoftCentric, Tech Mahindra and Aurachain; (7) Romanian trade press in Romanian (ZF, Wall-Street, Economedia, Nocash, Bancherul) for management statements. Baseline re-verified against primary sources: the 1,220 ATM + 264 MFM = 1,484 estate and the RON ~235m 2025 digital spend are both confirmed verbatim in the 30/04/2026 CEC results release; the 5 Digital Agency pilots are confirmed and are STILL only five as of the 26/06/2026 page update, with expansion stated but unquantified; Temenos still has no announced go-live. Genuine gaps: (a) H1-2026 interim results are not published yet (CEC has historically posted interim IFRS statements around October), so no 2026 fleet or capex update exists; (b) the ATM/MFM OEM remains unidentified after four distinct attempts - the bank has consistently refused to name it since 2020; (c) no equipment vendor is disclosed for the Digital Agency pilots; (d) IT/software capex lines for 2025 could not be read because the FY2025 statutory PDFs are image scans.
access_issues: www.cec.ro returns HTTP 403 to the plain fetch tool on every page - worked around by re-requesting the same URLs with a desktop Chrome User-Agent via curl (all pages then returned 200). Article bodies on cec.ro are partly client-rendered; where the visible body was empty the text was recovered from the page's embedded JSON-LD 'description'/'datePublished' fields. https://www.consiliulconcurentei.ro/presa/ returned HTTP 503 even with a desktop User-Agent, so the per-bank ROBOR fine breakdown was taken from Economedia's live blog (press tier) rather than the regulator. https://ibsintelligence.com/... returned 403 to both the fetch tool and curl; the Aurachain fact was sourced from aurachain.ch instead. Two CEC statutory PDFs - 'Raportul Consiliului de Administratie 31.12.2025' (63 pages, 10.8 MB) and 'Situatii financiare IFRS la 31 dec. 2025' (12.4 MB) - are scanned images with no text layer; pdfminer returned 63 and 5 characters respectively. bvb.ro instrument pages timed out. No source was silently dropped.
operator_requests: Please OCR two CEC Bank PDFs that are image-only scans and extract (i) intangible-asset/software additions and property-and-equipment additions for 2025, (ii) any ATM/MFM/POS or branch-count table, (iii) any named IT supplier or outsourcing arrangement: https://www.cec.ro/sites/default/files/2026-05/Raportul%20Consiliului%20de%20Administratie_CEC%20Bank_%2031.12.2025.pdf and https://www.cec.ro/sites/default/files/2026-05/Situatii%20financiare%20IFRS%20la%2031%20dec.2025.pdf . Also, if an operator can reach consiliulconcurentei.ro (503 to us), retrieve the official ROBOR decision press release and any published decision text confirming CEC Bank's RON 332.98m fine.
